record.original_question: Let R and S be left-linear term-rewriting systems over disjoint vocabularies. If each system has unicity of normal forms with respect to reduction, meaning any two normal forms reachable by reduction from the same term are identical, must the union R union S also have unicity of normal forms with respect to reduction?

evidence.quote: Is unicity of normal forms with respect to reduction a modular property of left-linear term-rewriting systems?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A term-rewriting system (TRS) consists of a signature (a set of function symbols, each with a fixed arity), a denumerable set of variables, and a set of rewrite rules l → r, where l and r are terms built from the signature and variables, l is not a variable, and every variable occurring in r also occurs in l. The one-step reduction relation →_R is defined as usual: s →_R t if t is obtained from s by replacing a subterm σ(l) by σ(r) for some rule l → r in R and some substitution σ. The reduction relation →*_R is the reflexive–transitive closure of →_R. A term t is in normal form if no rewrite step applies to it. A TRS R is left-linear if, in every rule l → r, no variable occurs more than once in l. A TRS R has unique normal forms with respect to reduction (the property UN→) if, whenever a term s satisfies s →*_R t₁ and s →*_R t₂ with both t₁ and t₂ in normal form, then t₁ = t₂.

Two TRSs R and S are said to have disjoint vocabularies if their signatures share no function symbol. Their union R ∪ S is the TRS whose signature is the disjoint union of the two signatures and whose rules are the union of the rules of R and S, applied to terms over the combined signature.

Decide: if R and S are left-linear TRSs over disjoint vocabularies and each of R and S has the property UN→, must the union R ∪ S also have the property UN→?
artifact.status_search_result: The question "Is unicity of normal forms with respect to reduction a modular property of left-linear term-rewriting systems?" is listed on the RTA List of Open Problems (originated by Middeldorp) and has been marked as solved. Subsequent literature on modularity of UN→ confirms a negative answer (counterexamples exist when left-linearity alone is assumed, although positive modularity results hold under additional restrictions such as non-collapsingness).
